en: The Section on Detailed Exposition, Chapter Seven: Convergence (Sampāta)
The Sequence of the Modes of Conveying: Herein, what is the sequence of the mode of conveying by way of turning back (*āvaṭṭa*)?
It is the verse beginning: “Therefore, for one whose mind is guarded, the range is right intention.”
“Therefore, for one whose mind is guarded, the domain is right intention” refers to serenity (*samatha*).
“Having right view as the foremost” refers to insight (*vipassanā*).
“Having known arising and passing away” refers to the full understanding of suffering (*dukkhapariññā*).
“A bhikkhu who has overcome sloth and torpor” refers to the abandoning of the origin [of suffering].
“May he abandon all miserable destinies” refers to cessation.
The application, the turning back, and the sequence of the modes are concluded.
